docs.title: GRC Power BI dashboard template
docs.text:
A reusable Power BI template for an executive ISO 27001 continual improvement and internal audit dashboard, fed from a single Excel workbook (typically a Continual Improvement Plan).

This site is the documentation for a design and build kit, not a pre-built .pbix. Use it to stand up a four-page executive report from a well-structured workbook, then point the same model at your own data.

All placeholders are generic (<Entity>, <Country>, <Owner>). There is no client or organisation-specific content. Every sample record is clearly marked as fictional.

docs.title: What you get
docs.text:
• A source workbook specification and a column-mapping table to complete against your own headings
  • A star-schema data model and example Power Query (M) scripts
  • A full DAX measure set
  • A four-page report specification
  • Configurable risk-candidate rules and a heat-map method
  • An executive colour theme, including a valid Power BI theme file
  • Fictional sample data so you can prototype before connecting a live workbook
  • A step-by-step Desktop build, publishing and reuse checklist

docs.title: Quick start
docs.text:
1. Download the sample workbook (or clone the repository).
  2. Fill in the column-mapping table in the source workbook specification against your real workbook.
  3. Open Power BI Desktop, create the parameters from the Power Query examples, and add the remaining queries.
  4. Paste the measures from measures.dax into the model.
  5. Import powerbi-theme.json (View → Browse for themes).
  6. Build the four report pages from the page specification.
  7. Work through the build checklist before publishing.

If your column names differ, keep the mapping table as the single source of truth and rename columns in Power Query. Leave the DAX names and page specifications unchanged where you can.

docs.title: What the dashboard is for
docs.text:
Leadership should be able to see, at a glance:

  • How many findings are open, overdue and closed on time
  • Where findings sit by type (nonconformity, opportunity for improvement, gap, observation), severity and entity
  • Whether named owners are closing actions to target — a direct measure of whether change is actually happening
  • Which strategic risk themes are accumulating findings, and which are credible candidates for the risk register
  • How control maturity compares across entities, and where low maturity coincides with open nonconformities

ISO 27001 asks whether a process exists. This dashboard is designed to show whether the process is changing anything.

docs.title: Design principles
docs.text:
• Generic and reusable. Swap the workbook path, sheet names and column map. Leave measures and page layouts alone where possible.
  • Star schema. Fact tables connect through shared dimensions (Date, Control, Entity, Owner, Risk Theme). Do not relate the two fact tables to each other.
  • Evidence over assertion. Measures prefer dates and status over narrative fields.
  • Promotion, not automation. Risk-candidate flags are decision support. A person still decides whether to raise an item on the risk register.

docs.title: Finding types
docs.text:
Code Meaning NC Nonconformity — a control or requirement is not met OFI Opportunity for improvement — the control works, but could be stronger Gap A required control or process is missing or incomplete OBS Observation — a noteworthy point that is not (yet) an NC or OFI

These codes are the template default. If your workbook uses different labels, map them in Power Query to these four values so the measures keep working.

docs.title: Licence and disclaimer
docs.text:
Released under the MIT Licence.

This template is a technical starting point for a management-system dashboard. It is not legal, audit or certification advice. Sample data is entirely fictional and must not be used as live evidence.

Comments on each page of this site are stored as GitHub Discussions (via giscus).

docs.title: Source workbook specification
docs.text:
The dashboard is designed around one Excel workbook, typically called Continual Improvement Plan. The template expects four worksheets. Two are required for the core model; two are strongly recommended and are used for the risk heat map and ownership page.

All names below are canonical names. Your live workbook may differ. Use the column-mapping table to record the actual headings and rename to these names in Power Query.

Placeholder tokens used in this kit:

  • <Entity> — the organisational unit the finding or maturity score belongs to (country, region, business unit or legal entity)
  • <Country> — used in the sample as the entity grain (United Kingdom, Spain, France, Germany). Replace with whatever grain you report on.
  • <Owner> — the person accountable for closing the finding
  • <Control ID> — an ISO 27001:2022 Annex A control identifier such as 8.5

Sample files in sample-data/ are fictional and labelled as such in every row (Data_Flag = Fictional sample).

docs.title: Sheet 1 — Internal Audit Findings (required)
docs.text:
This is the main fact table. One row equals one finding.

Canonical column Type Required Notes Finding_ID Text Yes Unique identifier, for example IA-2026-014 Finding_Title Text Yes Short name shown in tables and tooltips Finding_Type Text Yes One of NC, OFI, Gap, OBS (see README) Severity Text Yes One of Critical, High, Medium, Low Control_ID Text Yes ISO 27001:2022 Annex A id, for example 5.19 or 8.8 Entity Text Yes <Entity> / <Country> the finding was raised against Owner_ID Text Yes Key to the Owners sheet Owner_Name Text No Convenience copy; the Owners dimension is authoritative Raised_Date Date Yes Date the finding was raised Target_Date Date Yes Agreed closure date Status Text Yes One of Open, In Progress, Closed Closed_Date Date Conditional Required when Status = Closed; leave blank otherwise Risk_Theme_ID Text Yes Key to the Risk Theme Mapping sheet (or a theme code you maintain) Risk_Theme Text No Convenience copy of the theme name Description Text No Longer narrative; useful in tooltips and drill-through Root_Cause Text No If captured Source Text No For example Internal audit, Surveillance audit, Management review, Incident review Auditor Text No Person or team who raised it Data_Flag Text Sample only In the sample file this is always Fictional sample. Remove or ignore in live use.

Validation rules (recommend enforcing in Excel or Power Query):

  • Finding_ID is unique and not blank.
  • Finding_Type, Severity and Status use only the allowed values (or a documented synonym that you map).
  • Closed_Date is blank if Status is not Closed, and is on or after Raised_Date.
  • Target_Date is on or after Raised_Date.
  • Every Control_ID exists in Annex A (or in your Statement of Applicability).
  • Every Owner_ID exists on the Owners sheet.
  • Every Risk_Theme_ID exists on the Risk Theme Mapping sheet.

docs.title: Sheet 2 — Control Maturity (required)
docs.text: One row per control. Maturity and related evidence are repeated as country (or entity) blocks side by side. This is the layout most improvement-plan workbooks already use. Power Query unpivots the blocks into a tall fact table (one row per control per entity). See powerquery/03-control-maturity.m and docs/02-data-model.md.

docs.title: Shared columns (left-hand side)
docs.text: Canonical column Type Required Notes Control_ID Text Yes ISO 27001:2022 Annex A id Control_Name Text Yes Short control title Annex_Category Text No Organizational, People, Physical or Technological

docs.title: Repeated block for each <Country> / <Entity>
docs.text:
Repeat the following columns once per entity. In the sample the prefixes are UK_, Spain_, France_ and Germany_. Replace prefixes with your own entity codes, and update the unpivot list in Power Query.

Canonical suffix Type Required Notes _Maturity Whole number Yes Integer 1–5 (see scale below) _Open_NC Whole number Yes Count of open or in-progress nonconformities for this control in this entity. Prefer a formula that counts from the Findings sheet so the two tabs cannot drift. _Open_OFI Whole number Yes Count of open or in-progress opportunities for improvement _Linked_Risk Text No Existing risk-register id if one is already linked, for example R-014. Leave blank if none.

Optional suffixes you may add and unpivot in the same way: _Open_Gap, _Open_OBS, _Last_Assessed, _Assessor, _Comments.

docs.title: Maturity scale (template default)
docs.text:
Score Rating Meaning 1 Informal Ad hoc practice; little or no documentation 2 Documented Policy or process exists, but operation is inconsistent 3 Implemented Operated consistently in the entity 4 Measured Operated and monitored, with evidence and KRIs 5 Improving Measured, reviewed and demonstrably improving

Risk-candidate rule 3 treats a score of 2 or below plus an open NC as a candidate. If you use a different scale, change the threshold in docs/04-risk-candidate-rules.md and in the DAX.

docs.title: Sheet 3 — Risk Theme Mapping (recommended)
docs.text:
Maps each Annex A control to one strategic risk theme. The heat map and the risk-candidate rules aggregate at this grain, not at individual control level (although control-level drill-through is still available).

If your workbook does not yet have this sheet, create it. Assigning a theme after the fact in Power Query is possible but harder to govern.

Canonical column Type Required Notes Control_ID Text Yes Annex A id (one row per control in the simple mapping) Control_Name Text No Convenience copy Annex_Category Text No Organizational / People / Physical / Technological Risk_Theme_ID Text Yes Stable code, for example RT-01 Risk_Theme Text Yes Display name, for example Access control and identity Theme_Description Text No One-sentence definition of the theme Default_Likelihood Whole number No 1–5 planning value used when a theme is promoted to the risk register Default_Impact Whole number No 1–5 planning value Data_Flag Text Sample only Fictional sample in the sample file

A control should map to one primary theme. If you genuinely need many-to-many, add a bridge table rather than duplicating fact rows.

docs.title: Suggested theme catalogue (edit freely)
docs.text:
These are generic information-security themes suitable for most ISO 27001 programmes. Rename or replace them to match your risk-management framework.

ID Theme RT-01 Access control and identity RT-02 Third-party and supply chain RT-03 Data protection and confidentiality RT-04 Vulnerability and technical hygiene RT-05 Human factor and awareness RT-06 Incident response and resilience RT-07 Asset and change management RT-08 Cloud and emerging technology RT-09 Physical and environmental security RT-10 Compliance and assurance

docs.title: Sheet 4 — Owners (recommended)
docs.text:
Lookup of finding owners. Used on the Ownership page (open / overdue / on-time performance) and for escalation labels.

Canonical column Type Required Notes Owner_ID Text Yes Unique key, referenced by Findings Owner_Name Text Yes Display name (<Owner>) Role Text Yes For example Information Security Lead, IT Operations, Data Protection Officer Entity Text Yes Home <Entity> / <Country>, or Group for a central function Function Text No For example Information security, IT, People, Procurement, Internal audit Email Text No Use a generic address pattern in examples Line_Manager Text No Name or id of the person overdue items escalate to Data_Flag Text Sample only Fictional sample in the sample file

docs.title: Optional extra columns and tabs
docs.text: The four tabs above are enough to build every page in this template. If your workbook already has further sheets (corrective actions, exceptions, incidents, training), leave them out of this model unless you have a clear visual that needs them. Do not relate those facts directly to Findings or Control Maturity; add them as additional facts on the same dimensions.

docs.title: File handling notes
docs.text:
• Keep a single current workbook path (or SharePoint URL) and store it in the pWorkbookPath parameter, not hard-coded in every query.
  • If the workbook is on SharePoint or OneDrive, use the SharePoint folder or Web connector rather than a personal C:\Users\... path, otherwise refresh will fail for everyone else.
  • Do not merge cells, and keep row 1 as a header row with no banner above it. Put the “fictional sample” warning in a column (Data_Flag) or in this documentation, not in a title row that breaks ingest.
  • Dates should be true Excel dates. The sample uses the ISO format yyyy-mm-dd in the CSV copies.

docs.title: Data model
docs.text:
The model is a star schema with two fact tables and five shared dimensions. The two facts are never related to each other. Filters flow from dimensions to facts. This keeps measures predictable when a slicer on entity, control, owner, theme or date is used.

                    ┌──────────────┐
                    │  Dim Date    │
                    └──────┬───────┘
                           │
         Raised / Target / Closed / Assessed (see relationships)
                           │
┌─────────────┐     ┌──────┴───────┐     ┌─────────────────────┐
│ Dim Control ├─────► Fact Findings │     │ Fact ControlMaturity│
└─────────────┘     └──────┬───────┘     └──────────┬──────────┘
                           │                         │
┌─────────────┐            │            ┌────────────┘
│ Dim Entity  ├────────────┼────────────┤
└─────────────┘            │            │
┌─────────────┐            │            │
│ Dim Owner   ├────────────┘            │
└─────────────┘                         │
┌─────────────┐                         │
│ Dim Risk    ├─────────────────────────┘  (via Control, or denormalised theme key)
│ Theme       │
└─────────────┘

The authoritative relationship view is the mermaid diagram below.

docs.title: Fact Findings
docs.text:
Loaded from Internal Audit Findings. Grain: one finding. This is the primary fact for pages 1–4.

Do not leave typographic synonyms in Finding_Type, Severity or Status. Map them once in Power Query to the canonical lists in docs/01-source-workbook-spec.md.

Calculated columns (or equivalent measures — see dax/measures.dax) are added after load:

  • Age_Days
  • Days_to_Close
  • Is_Overdue
  • Closed_On_Time
  • Ageing_Bucket

docs.title: Fact Control Maturity
docs.text:
Loaded from Control Maturity after unpivoting the entity blocks. Grain: one control + one entity.

Column Type Notes Control_ID Text Key to Dim Control Entity Text Key to Dim Entity (prefix translated to the display name) Maturity Whole number 1–5 Open_NC Whole number Prefer to treat as stored evidence; you can also reconcile to Findings with a measure Open_OFI Whole number Linked_Risk Text Existing risk-register id, if any

If your prefixes differ, edit the prefix list in powerquery/03-control-maturity.m.

docs.title: Dim Date
docs.text:
Built in Power Query from a start and end date (see powerquery/04-date-table.m). Mark as the official date table in Power BI.

Recommended range: 1 January of the earliest Raised_Date year, through 31 December of next year (or Date.EndOfYear(DateTime.LocalNow()) + 1 year).

Useful columns: Date, Year, Quarter, QuarterName, MonthNumber, MonthName, YearMonth, YearMonthSort, WeekOfYear, DayOfWeek, DayName, IsWorkingDay (Mon–Fri, no public-holiday calendar unless you add one), FiscalYear and FiscalQuarter with a 1 April start (common in the UK; change the start month if needed).

docs.title: Dim Control
docs.text:
Distinct Annex A controls. In the sample this is derived from the Risk Theme Mapping sheet (one row per control, with its primary theme). You can also maintain a static controls table.

Columns: Control_ID, Control_Name, Annex_Category, Risk_Theme_ID.

docs.title: Dim Entity
docs.text:
Small lookup of reporting entities. In the sample: United Kingdom, Spain, France, Germany, plus Group for central owners.

Columns: Entity, Entity_Code, Entity_Sort (to keep a stable column order in matrices).

docs.title: Dim Owner
docs.text: Loaded from the Owners sheet. Columns as specified in the workbook spec. Relate Owner_ID to Findings. An optional, inactive or many-to-one relationship from Dim Owner[Entity] to Dim Entity[Entity] can be used for “owners based in this country” filters; do not make it active if it would create ambiguity with the finding’s own entity.

docs.title: Dim Risk Theme
docs.text:
Distinct themes from the mapping sheet: Risk_Theme_ID, Risk_Theme, Theme_Description, Default_Likelihood, Default_Impact.

Control-to-theme is already on Dim Control, so Fact Control Maturity inherits a theme through Control. Findings also carry Risk_Theme_ID directly so a finding remains filterable even if its control mapping later changes. Keep the two in step in the source workbook.

docs.title: Relationships
docs.text:
Create these in Model view. All are single-direction (dimension filters fact) unless noted.

From (1) To (*) On Active? Purpose Dim Date[Date] Fact Findings[Raised_Date] Date Yes Default time intelligence: when findings were raised Dim Date[Date] Fact Findings[Target_Date] Date No Use with USERELATIONSHIP for “due in this period” Dim Date[Date] Fact Findings[Closed_Date] Date No Use with USERELATIONSHIP for “closed in this period” Dim Control[Control_ID] Fact Findings[Control_ID] Text Yes Dim Control[Control_ID] Fact Control Maturity[Control_ID] Text Yes Dim Entity[Entity] Fact Findings[Entity] Text Yes Dim Entity[Entity] Fact Control Maturity[Entity] Text Yes Dim Owner[Owner_ID] Fact Findings[Owner_ID] Text Yes Dim Risk Theme[Risk_Theme_ID] Fact Findings[Risk_Theme_ID] Text Yes Dim Risk Theme[Risk_Theme_ID] Dim Control[Risk_Theme_ID] Text Yes Lets theme slicers reach maturity via Control

Do not create a relationship between Fact Findings and Fact Control Maturity. If you need “maturity of the control this finding sits on”, use TREATAS or a measure that looks up via Control and Entity, as in dax/measures.dax.

Hide technical keys from Report view once relationships are in place (Finding_ID may stay visible because it is useful on drill-through).

docs.title: Power Query steps (overview)
docs.text:
Detailed M is in powerquery/. The intended sequence is:

  1. Create parameters — workbook path and the four sheet names (01-parameters.m).
  2. Staging — one “raw” query per sheet, with columns renamed to canonical names using your mapping table. Set types. Remove the Data_Flag column in live use, or leave it and filter it out of visuals.
  3. Fact Findings — clean lists, trim text, fix dates, add a quality query (duplicates, missing keys) that you can keep disabled.
  4. Fact Control Maturity — unpivot entity blocks:
  5. Hold the shared columns (Control_ID, Control_Name, Annex_Category).
  6. Unpivot all other columns to Attribute, Value.
  7. Split Attribute into Entity_Code and Metric on the first underscore (or on your chosen delimiter).
  8. Map Entity_Code to the Dim Entity display name.
  9. Pivot Metric back to Maturity, Open_NC, Open_OFI, Linked_Risk.
  10. Set types.
  11. Dim Date — generate with List.Dates.
  12. Dimensions — distinct Control, Entity, Owner, Risk Theme. Disable load on staging queries; enable load only on facts and dims.

Refresh should be one click once the parameter points at the live file.

docs.title: Alternative layouts
docs.text:
If your maturity sheet is already tall (one row per control per entity), skip the unpivot and load it directly as Fact Control Maturity.

If you report on business units rather than countries, treat them as entities. Nothing in the DAX depends on the entity being a country.

docs.title: Naming conventions
docs.text:
• Fact tables: Fact Findings, Fact Control Maturity
  • Dimensions: Dim Date, Dim Control, Dim Entity, Dim Owner, Dim Risk Theme
  • Measures live in a display folder, grouped as _Base, Ageing, Types, Maturity, Ownership, Risk
  • Prefix hidden helper measures with _ so they sort together

docs.title: Report pages
docs.text:
Four pages, in this order. The theme in theme/powerbi-theme.json and the RAG rules in docs/05-theme-and-style.md apply to all of them.

Common conventions:

  • Page size: 16:9 (1280 × 720) unless you are designing for a specific wallboard.
  • Global slicers (sync across pages): Entity, Year (from Raised Date), Finding Type, Severity, Risk Theme. Put them in a slim left rail or a top bar and keep the same position on every page.
  • As-at date: show a small label “As at \<today>” using the As At Date measure, so a printed or exported pack is dated.
  • Tooltips: every chart should have a report-page or default tooltip that includes Finding Type, Severity, Entity, Owner and Target Date where it is meaningful.
  • Drill-through: pages 1–3 drill through to a hidden Finding Detail layout (specified at the bottom of this file). Page 4 also drills through to the same layout, filtered to the theme or control.
  • No client branding in the template. Add your organisation header later if you need it.

docs.title: Page 1 — Executive Summary
docs.text: Purpose. A single leadership view: are we closing findings, is maturity acceptable, and where should attention go this quarter?

docs.title: Cards (KPI row)
docs.text: Visual Measure RAG Open findings Open Findings Neutral count; optional colour if above a threshold you set Overdue findings Overdue Findings Green = 0; Amber = 1–4; Red = 5+ (adjust in the theme or conditional formatting) % closed on time % Closed On Time Green ≥ 80%; Amber 60–79%; Red < 60% Average days to close Avg Days to Close Green ≤ 45; Amber 46–90; Red > 90 (targets are configurable)

docs.title: Other visuals
docs.text:
Visual Fields / measures Notes Clustered bar — maturity by entity Axis: Dim Entity[Entity]; Value: Avg Maturity Score; optional reference line at 3 Sort by Entity_Sort. Tooltip: % Controls Mature, Controls Below Target, Open NC (maturity fact) Stacked bar — open findings by type and entity Axis: Entity; Legend: Finding Type; Value: Open Findings Keep the type colour map in the theme (NC red, Gap orange, OFI amber, OBS slate) Combination — raised vs closed by month Axis: Dim Date[YearMonth] via the active Raised relationship for one series; use the closed-date measures with USERELATIONSHIP for the other Add a tooltip with net movement (Raised in Period − Closed in Period) Donut or stacked bar — open findings by severity Legend: Severity; Value: Open Findings Table — attention list Finding ID, Title, Type, Severity, Entity, Owner, Target Date, Days Overdue, Is Risk Candidate Filter to overdue, or Critical/High and open, or risk candidates. Top N 10 by days overdue. Enable drill-through

docs.title: Page 2 — Findings by Type
docs.text: Purpose. Break the portfolio down by type, severity and age, then drill to the list.

docs.title: Layout sketch
docs.text:
┌──────── Title: Findings by type                                                      ┐
│ Slicers (synced)                                                                      │
├───────────────────────────────┬───────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤

│ Open Gap | Open OBS           │  values = Open Findings; subtotals on                 │

├───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤

│ ID, Title, Type, Severity, Control, Entity, Owner, Raised, Target, Status, Age days   │

docs.title: Visuals
docs.text:
Visual Fields / measures Notes Four cards Open NC, Open OFI, Open Gap, Open OBS Also show a small comparison to closed counts in the tooltip Matrix Rows: Finding Type; Columns: Severity; Values: Open Findings; Show values as: optional % of row Add Entity as a second row level, or as a slicer only, if the matrix becomes crowded. Conditional format cells on count (white → navy) Stacked bar — ageing Axis: Ageing Bucket (sort with Ageing Bucket Sort); Legend: Finding Type; Value: Open Findings Closed items are excluded by the measure. Over-90 should visually dominate if the “slow change” problem is present Detail table See sketch Conditional format: Status, Severity, Ageing. Right-click drill-through to Finding Detail

Page or visual filter: none required; measures already distinguish open vs closed. Offer a Status slicer on this page only if reviewers want to inspect closed items in the table.

docs.title: Page 3 — Ownership
docs.text: Purpose. Show whether named owners are closing work to target. This is the page that makes slow change visible.

docs.title: Layout sketch
docs.text:
┌──────── Title: Ownership and accountability                                          ┐
│ Slicers (synced)                                                                      │
├────────────────────────────────────┬──────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ Owner scorecard (table)            │  Top 10 overdue owners (bar)                     │
│ Owner, Role, Entity, Open,         │  Value: Overdue Findings                         │
│ Overdue, % on time, Avg days       │  Axis: Owner Name                                │
├────────────────────────────────────┴──────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ Overdue findings by owner and type (stacked bar)                                      │
├────────────────────────────────────┬──────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ Ageing by owner (matrix)           │  Escalation table: overdue > 60 days             │
│ Owner × Ageing bucket              │  Owner, Line manager, Finding, Target, Days over │
└────────────────────────────────────┴──────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

docs.title: Visuals
docs.text:
Visual Fields / measures Notes Owner scorecard table Dim Owner[Owner_Name], Role, Entity, Open Findings, Overdue Findings, Owner % On Time, Avg Days to Close, Closed Findings Conditional format % On Time and Overdue with the same RAG as page 1. Sort by Overdue desc, then Open desc Top 10 overdue owners Axis: Owner Name; Value: Overdue Findings Filter out zeros. This is the “change is not happening” visual Stacked bar — overdue by owner and type Axis: Owner; Legend: Type; Value: Overdue Findings Matrix — ageing by owner Rows: Owner; Columns: Ageing bucket; Values: Open Findings Colour the Over 90 column red when > 0 Escalation table Owner, Line Manager, Finding ID, Title, Entity, Target Date, Days Overdue Visual-level filter: Days Overdue ≥ 60 (threshold is configurable; see risk-candidate rules). Intended as a pack you can export for the management review

Do not use “unassigned” as a hidden bucket. Findings with a missing owner should appear as (Unassigned) so the gap is visible.

docs.title: Page 4 — Risk Heat Map and Risk Candidates
docs.text: Purpose. Aggregate findings into strategic risk themes, place each theme on a likelihood × impact heat map, and list which themes or controls are candidates for the risk register. Candidates are a recommendation, not an automatic register entry. See docs/04-risk-candidate-rules.md.

docs.title: Layout sketch
docs.text:
┌──────── Title: Risk heat map and risk candidates                                     ┐
│ Slicers (synced) + optional “Candidates only” slicer                                  │
├─────────────────────────────────────┬─────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ Heat map matrix                     │  Cards: Candidate themes | Candidate findings   │
│ Rows: Risk Theme                    │         | Themes with no linked risk            │
│ Columns: Impact (1–5)  — or a 5×5   │                                                 │
│ of Likelihood (rows) × Impact (cols)│                                                 │
│ Values: Heat Map Score / count      │                                                 │
│ Colour: RAG bands                   │                                                 │
├─────────────────────────────────────┴─────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ Candidate table                                                                       │
│ Theme or Control, Entities affected, Open NC, Repeat flag, Age flag, Maturity flag,   │
│ Cluster flag, Candidate Score, Linked Risk, Recommended action                        │
├───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ Supporting bar: open findings by theme (stacked by type)                              │
└───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

docs.title: Heat map construction
docs.text:
Two valid layouts; pick one and stay consistent.

Option A (recommended for executives). One row per risk theme. Columns: Derived Likelihood, Derived Impact, Heat Map Score, Open Findings, Open NC, Is Risk Candidate, Linked Risk Count. Conditional-format the score column on the 1–25 scale (see RAG in the theme document). This is easier to read than a sparse 5×5.

Option B (classic 5×5). Matrix with Likelihood 1–5 on rows (or columns) and Impact 1–5 on the other axis. Value = count of themes (or Heat Map Score) falling in that cell. Put a theme table next to it so a cell can be selected and the list filters. Derived likelihood and impact come from the measures in dax/measures.dax, not from a manual plot unless you override them.

Derived axes (defaults, documented in the rules file):

  • Likelihood rises with recurrence (open findings in the theme, and whether the same NC appears in two or more entities).
  • Impact rises with severity (weighted: Critical 4, High 3, Medium 2, Low 1) and with low maturity.

docs.title: Candidate table
docs.text:
Column Source Risk Theme (and/or Control ID + name) Dimensions Entities affected Entities With Open NC Open NC / Open OFI / Open OBS Type measures Repeat NC (≥ 2 entities) Flag Repeat NC Open > 90 days or overdue Flag Ageing Maturity ≤ 2 and open NC Flag Low Maturity NC ≥ 3 OFI/OBS in theme Flag Cluster Candidate score (0–100) Risk Candidate Score Already on register? Linked Risk from the maturity fact, or a count Recommended action Candidate Recommendation (text measure)

A theme or control is a candidate when any of the four flags is true. Score is a weighted combination, so a theme can be a mild or a strong candidate. Sort this table by score descending.

Governance note on the page itself. Add a static text box:

Risk-candidate flags are decision support for the risk workshop. Promoting a candidate to the risk register remains a management decision, with an owner, treatment and review date.

docs.title: Hidden page — Finding Detail (drill-through)
docs.text:
Create a hidden page with drill-through filters on Finding_ID (and keep Entity, Theme and Control as extra drill-through fields so cards on pages 1–4 can also land here).

Layout: a single-finding card (title, type, severity, status, dates, owner, line manager, control, theme, description, root cause) plus a small context visual (“other open findings on this control / this owner / this theme”).

Enable “Keep all filters” if you want the source slicers to travel with the drill-through; otherwise leave it off so the context visuals can show the wider picture.

docs.title: Interaction and usability notes
docs.text:
• Turn off cross-highlight on the KPI cards so selecting a bar does not blank the cards unexpectedly; use cross-filter from the heat map and type visuals onto the tables.
  • Use a tool-tip page (optional) that shows the top five open findings in the hovered context.
  • Bookmark a “reset slicers” button if you have many synced slicers.
  • Export: the owner scorecard and the escalation table should be easy to export to Excel for the management review pack.

docs.title: Risk-candidate rules
docs.text:
These rules decide when a control or a strategic risk theme is a good candidate to discuss as a risk — typically at a risk workshop or management review — rather than leaving it only as an audit finding.

They are decision support, not an automatic posting to the risk register. A candidate still needs an owner, a treatment, a likelihood and impact that management accepts, and a review date, before it becomes a live risk.

All thresholds below are parameters. Keep the numeric values in one place in DAX (_Param * measures in dax/measures.dax) so you can change them without rewriting the rules.

docs.title: Why findings are not automatically risks
docs.text: A finding is evidence about a control at a point in time. A risk is an uncertain event or condition that could affect objectives, with a treatment plan. Promote a finding (or a cluster of them) when the evidence suggests the issue is systemic, persistent, or material — not when it is a one-off documentation slip that is already being closed.

docs.title: The four default criteria
docs.text: A control or theme is a risk candidate if any of the following is true. The candidate score (0–100) then reflects how many criteria fire and how severe they are.

docs.title: 1. Repeat nonconformities across entities
docs.text:
Rule. There is an open or in-progress NC against the same Control_ID (theme-level: against controls in the same theme) in two or more entities.

Default threshold. ≥ 2 entities (_Param Repeat Entity Threshold).

Rationale. The same NC in more than one <Entity> is a strong signal that the issue is in the management system, not in a single local process. These are usually the best candidates.

Flag measure. Flag Repeat NC

docs.title: 2. Persistent or overdue findings
docs.text:
Rule. There is at least one open or in-progress NC that is either:

  • past its Target_Date (overdue), or
  • open for longer than 90 days from Raised_Date, even if the target is still in the future.

Default thresholds. Overdue = target date < today; ageing = 90 days (_Param Persistent Days).

Rationale. Slow closure is itself a risk: the original control weakness remains, and the improvement process is not working at the pace the ISMS claims.

Flag measure. Flag Ageing

You may tighten this to “any finding type, not only NC” if your appetite is low. The default stays on NCs so observations and OFIs do not inflate the register.

docs.title: 3. Low maturity with an open nonconformity
docs.text:
Rule. For a given control and entity, Maturity ≤ 2 (Documented or Informal) and Open_NC ≥ 1.

Default threshold. Maturity ≤ 2 (_Param Low Maturity).

Rationale. A documented-but-not-operated control that already has an NC is exactly the “compliant on paper, not in practice” pattern. At theme level, the flag fires if any in-scope control–entity pair meets the rule.

Flag measure. Flag Low Maturity NC

This is the one rule that needs the Control Maturity fact. If maturity data is missing for a control, do not fire the flag; report the gap in a data-quality measure instead.

docs.title: 4. Clustered opportunities and observations
docs.text:
Rule. There are three or more open or in-progress OFI or OBS (combined) in the same risk theme.

Default threshold. ≥ 3 (_Param Cluster Threshold). Gaps may be included by adding them to the measure; the default leaves Gaps out, because a Gap is often already treated as closer to an NC and should be considered under rules 1–3 if it is one.

Rationale. A single OFI is a local improvement. A cluster on one theme usually means a systemic weakness that nobody has yet called a nonconformity.

Flag measure. Flag Cluster

docs.title: Candidate score
docs.text:
The score is a 0–100 index used to sort the candidate table, not a likelihood or impact rating.

Default weights (must sum to 100):

Criterion Weight Additional severity bump Repeat NC across entities 35 +5 if 3+ entities, +5 if any Critical NC Persistent / overdue NC 25 +5 if any item is more than 180 days open or more than 60 days overdue Low maturity + open NC 25 +5 if any maturity is 1 (Informal) Clustered OFI / OBS 15 +5 if 6 or more in the theme

Capped at 100. A score of 0 means no criterion fired. Interpret roughly as:

Score Meaning 0 Not a candidate under current rules 1–40 Mild candidate — discuss, often treat as a grouped action rather than a new risk 41–70 Firm candidate — take to the risk workshop with a proposed owner 71–100 Strong candidate — typically already overdue or repeating; escalate if not already on the register

The text measure Candidate Recommendation returns one of: Not a candidate, Discuss as grouped action, Workshop — propose risk, Escalate — strong candidate.

docs.title: Likelihood and impact for the heat map
docs.text: Do not confuse the candidate score with heat-map likelihood and impact. The heat map is a 5×5 plot of themes, using derived values so a first draft exists even before the risk workshop.

docs.title: Derived likelihood (1–5)
docs.text:
Based on recurrence and persistence of open items in the theme:

Condition (evaluated top-down; first match wins) Likelihood Repeat NC in 3 or more entities, or 5+ open NCs in the theme 5 Repeat NC in 2 entities, or 3–4 open NCs, or any NC open > 90 days 4 1–2 open NCs, or a cluster of OFI/OBS (≥ 3) 3 Open findings exist, but no NC and no cluster 2 No open findings in the theme 1

If you prefer a formula instead of bands: start at 1, add 1 for any open finding, add 1 for any open NC, add 1 for repeat-entity NCs, add 1 for persistent/overdue NCs, cap at 5.

docs.title: Derived impact (1–5)
docs.text:
Based on severity mix and the worst relevant maturity:

Condition (top-down) Impact Any open Critical finding, or maturity 1 with an open NC 5 Any open High finding, or maturity ≤ 2 with an open NC 4 Medium is the highest open severity, or 3+ open findings 3 Only Low open findings 2 No open findings 1

Alternatively, a weighted severity average (Critical 5, High 4, Medium 3, Low 2) rounded to the nearest integer, then raised by 1 if the low-maturity-plus-NC flag is true, capped at 5.

Default_Likelihood and Default_Impact on Dim Risk Theme are planning values for the register, not the derived heat-map axes. Use them as a starting point in the workshop if you disagree with the derived figures.

docs.title: Heat map score
docs.text:
Heat Map Score = Derived Likelihood × Derived Impact (range 1–25).

Score Band Colour 1–4 Low Green 5–9 Moderate Amber 10–16 High Orange / dark amber 17–25 Extreme Red

These bands should match your organisation’s risk matrix if you already have one. Change the breaks once, in DAX and in the theme documentation.

docs.title: Already on the register
docs.text: If Linked_Risk is populated on the maturity fact (or you later add a risk-register id on the finding), the candidate is labelled Already on register rather than “new candidate”. Keep it visible: the workshop should check that the treatment is actually moving, especially when flags are still firing.

docs.title: Promoting a candidate — governance
docs.text:
When a candidate is accepted:

  1. Assign a risk owner (often the theme owner, not necessarily the finding owner).
  2. Agree likelihood and impact (start from the derived values; record any override and the reason).
  3. Record the treatment, due date and expected evidence.
  4. Link the risk id back to the Control Maturity sheet (Linked_Risk) and, if you use it, to the finding.
  5. Leave the original findings open until their own closure criteria are met. Closing a finding because a risk was raised hides the control failure.
  6. Review overdue treatments at the same forum that reviews overdue findings, so the slow-change problem cannot be moved to a different register and forgotten.

When a candidate is rejected, record a short reason (for example “single-site issue, already in closure, residual accepted”). That record belongs in the workshop minutes, not in this dashboard, unless you add an exclusions table later.

docs.title: Tuning the rules
docs.text:
Change the _Param * measures first, then review the sample workbook to see whether the flags still tell a sensible story. Signs you need to retune:

  • Almost every theme is a candidate — thresholds are too tight, or the source data is messy (status not closed, dates missing).
  • Almost nothing is a candidate, despite known systemic issues — repeat-entity matching may be failing on inconsistent Control_ID or Entity spellings.
  • Clusters of OFIs never appear — check that type labels were mapped to OFI and OBS.

Revisit the parameters at least at each management review.

docs.title: Theme and style
docs.text:
The template uses a calm executive palette: deep navy for structure, a restrained set of data colours, and a strict red–amber–green (RAG) language for status. Import theme/powerbi-theme.json in Power BI Desktop via View → Browse for themes. The JSON is a valid Power BI report theme (named colours, text classes and a starter set of visual styles).

Do not add organisation or client branding to the shared template. You can fork the theme file later with a logo or extra colours if a specific report needs it.

docs.title: Structure
docs.text: Token Hex Use Navy #1B365D Titles, axis text, primary KPI colour, table accent Ink #3D4F61 Body labels, secondary text Muted #6B7C8A Axis lines, hints, footnotes Line #D0D5DA Gridlines, card borders Paper #FFFFFF Page and card background Wash #F4F6F8 Alternating table rows, slicer well, page background tint if you prefer off-white

docs.title: Data colours (applied in order)
docs.text: Order Hex Suggested meaning 1 #1B365D Navy — default series 2 #2E6B8A Steel blue 3 #4A9BB4 Teal 4 #7C9A6E Sage 5 #C4A35A Gold 6 #C05640 Rust 7 #6B7C8A Slate 8 #8B6B9A Plum

docs.title: Finding type (lock these, do not rely on series order)
docs.text:
Type Hex Notes NC #C62828 Red — nonconformity Gap #E65100 Deep orange OFI #F9A825 Amber OBS #546E7A Blue-grey

Set these explicitly in the visuals (or in visualStyles for column/bar charts) so a missing type does not cause colours to shuffle.

docs.title: Severity
docs.text: Severity Hex Critical #7B1113 High #C62828 Medium #F9A825 Low #546E7A

docs.title: RAG and diverging scales
docs.text:
Token Hex Theme key Use Good / Low risk #2E7D32 good, minimum On track, closed on time, maturity ≥ 4, heat map 1–4 Neutral / Moderate #F9A825 neutral, center Watch, on-time rate 60–79%, maturity = 3, heat map 5–9 High (heat map mid-high) #E65100 — Heat map 10–16; use as a manual conditional-format colour Bad / Extreme #C62828 bad, maximum Overdue, on-time rate < 60%, maturity ≤ 2, heat map 17–25

Power BI theme files expose good, neutral, bad and the diverging minimum / center / maximum keys. The extra orange for “high” (as opposed to “extreme”) is documented here for conditional formatting; it is also included in dataColors as rust/gold so it is available to the report.

docs.title: RAG rules (conditional formatting)
docs.text: Apply these consistently on every page. Thresholds match the defaults in docs/04-risk-candidate-rules.md and docs/03-report-pages.md; if you change a parameter in DAX, change the rule here and on the visual.

docs.title: KPI cards
docs.text: Measure Green Amber Red Overdue Findings 0 1–4 5+ % Closed On Time ≥ 80% 60–79% < 60% Avg Days to Close ≤ 45 46–90 > 90 Open Findings No colour by default Optional: amber above your agreed workload, red above a hard cap

docs.title: Maturity
docs.text: Score Rating Colour 1 Informal Red 2 Documented Red 3 Implemented Amber 4 Measured Green 5 Improving Green

docs.title: Ageing buckets (open items)
docs.text: Bucket Colour 0–30 days Green 31–60 days Amber 61–90 days Deep orange #E65100 Over 90 days Red

docs.title: Heat map score
docs.text: Score Band Colour 1–4 Low Green 5–9 Moderate Amber 10–16 High Deep orange #E65100 17–25 Extreme Red

docs.title: Candidate score
docs.text: Score Colour 0 No fill (not a candidate) 1–40 Amber 41–70 Deep orange 71–100 Red

docs.title: Typography
docs.text:
The theme file sets:

Class Font Size Colour Use Callout Segoe UI Semibold 44 Navy KPI values Title Segoe UI Semibold 16 Navy Visual titles Header Segoe UI Semibold 12 Navy Table / matrix headers Label Segoe UI 10 Ink Axes, card labels, slicers

If Segoe UI is not available (for example on some macOS authoring machines), Power BI falls back to a sans-serif system font. Do not use decorative or condensed fonts on an executive pack.

Page title: 20 pt Semibold, navy, top-left. “As at” date: 10 pt, muted, top-right.

docs.title: Visual style conventions
docs.text:
• Backgrounds: white visuals on a white or wash page. Hairline #D0D5DA border, 4 px corner radius, no drop shadow.
  • Gridlines: horizontal only, #D0D5DA, 1 px. No vertical gridlines on bar charts.
  • Legends: top-centre or bottom-centre, 9–10 pt, ink.
  • Data labels: prefer labels on KPI-adjacent bars; avoid labelling every point on a dense line.
  • Slicers: dropdown or tile, navy selected state, no search box unless a field is long (Owner, Control).
  • Tables: header navy text on wash; alternating rows #F4F6F8; totals in Semibold. Do not use total rows on the attention or escalation lists.
  • Empty states: “No items in this context” rather than a blank visual.

docs.title: Accessibility
docs.text:
• Do not rely on colour alone: overdue tables also show a Days Overdue number; candidate tables show flags as Yes/No, not only a colour.
  • Maintain contrast of at least 4.5:1 for body text (navy or ink on white meets this; muted grey on wash may not — use muted only for non-essential hints).
  • The NC red (#C62828) and OFI amber (#F9A825) are distinguishable by hue and brightness; test in greyscale if the pack will be printed in monochrome (type labels must remain visible).

docs.title: Importing and maintaining the theme
docs.text:
1. In Power BI Desktop: View → Themes → Browse for themes and select theme/powerbi-theme.json.
  2. Confirm the theme name ISO 27001 Continual Improvement — Executive appears in the theme gallery.
  3. After import, still set the locked type and severity colours on the first visual of each kind; some chart types do not pick categorical mappings from the theme file alone.
  4. If you edit the JSON, keep it valid UTF-8 JSON (no comments, no trailing commas) and re-import. A short checklist is in docs/06-build-checklist.md.

docs.title: Build checklist
docs.text:
Follow this once to stand the report up in Power BI Desktop, then use the reuse section when you point it at a different workbook.

Tick as you go. The sample workbook in sample-data/ is the safest first pass; switch the path parameter to a live file only after the model and pages look right.

docs.title: A. Prepare the source
docs.text:
• Read docs/01-source-workbook-spec.md and fill in the column-mapping table against your workbook (or confirm the sample already matches the canonical names).
  • Confirm the workbook has the two required tabs (Internal Audit Findings, Control Maturity) and, ideally, Risk Theme Mapping and Owners.
  • Check there is no banner row above the header, no merged cells in the used range, and that dates are true Excel dates.
  • Harmonise entity spellings (UK vs United Kingdom) and type/status synonyms, or plan to map them in Power Query.
  • If the live file will be refreshed by other people, place it on SharePoint or OneDrive, not a personal drive letter.

docs.title: B. Create the Power BI file
docs.text:
• Open Power BI Desktop and save the file as grc-continual-improvement-dashboard.pbix (or your own generic name) outside this repository. .pbix files are git-ignored on purpose.
  • File → Options → Current file → Data load: disable auto date/time tables (you will use Dim Date).
  • View → Browse for themes and import theme/powerbi-theme.json. Confirm the theme name appears.

docs.title: C. Parameters and queries
docs.text:
• Home → Transform data → Manage parameters → New parameter for each entry in powerquery/01-parameters.m:
  • pWorkbookPath (Text) — full path or SharePoint URL of the Excel file
  • pFindingsSheet (Text) — default Internal Audit Findings
  • pMaturitySheet (Text) — default Control Maturity
  • pThemesSheet (Text) — default Risk Theme Mapping
  • pOwnersSheet (Text) — default Owners
  • pStartDate / pEndDate (Date) — optional; otherwise the date table script derives them
  • Create a blank query for each script in powerquery/, paste the M, and name the queries exactly as in docs/02-data-model.md (Fact Findings, Fact Control Maturity, Dim Date, Dim Control, Dim Entity, Dim Owner, Dim Risk Theme).
  • Point any staging queries at the parameters, not at hard-coded paths.
  • For Control Maturity, confirm the entity prefix list in 03-control-maturity.m matches your column prefixes. Adjust and close the unpivot preview: you should see one row per control per entity, with Maturity, Open_NC, Open_OFI and Linked_Risk as columns.
  • Set data types (Date, Whole Number, Text) and rename any remaining source columns to canonical names.
  • Disable load on staging / helper queries. Enable load on the two facts and five dimensions.
  • Close & Apply. Fix any type or relationship errors before going further.

docs.title: D. Model view
docs.text:
• Create the relationships listed in docs/02-data-model.md. Only the Raised Date relationship to Dim Date should be active; Target Date and Closed Date are inactive.
  • Mark Dim Date as a date table (Table tools → Mark as date table), using the Date column.
  • Hide technical foreign keys from Report view, except Finding_ID if you want it on drill-through.
  • Confirm there is no relationship between the two fact tables.

docs.title: E. Measures and columns
docs.text:
• Create a measures table (empty table named _Measures is a common pattern) and paste groups from dax/measures.dax into display folders: _Parameters, _Base, Ageing, Types, Maturity, Ownership, Risk.
  • Add the calculated columns described in the DAX file (ageing bucket, overdue flag, closed-on-time) if you prefer columns over the equivalent measures for slicers and sorts.
  • Check the parameter measures (_Param Repeat Entity Threshold, _Param Persistent Days, _Param Low Maturity, _Param Cluster Threshold, and the KPI RAG thresholds) and change them if your policy differs from the defaults.
  • Put a few slicers on a scratch page and sanity-check:
  • Open Findings + Closed Findings equals Findings Count (when no status filter is applied).
  • Overdue Findings only includes open or in-progress items with Target_Date before today.
  • % Closed On Time only uses closed rows and compares Closed_Date to Target_Date.
  • Maturity averages change when you slice Entity, and stay blank rather than zero when a context has no rows.
  • Risk-candidate flags on the sample data fire for repeat NCs, aged NCs, low-maturity + NC, and clustered OFI/OBS (the sample is written so each rule has at least one hit).

docs.title: F. Report pages
docs.text:
Build in this order, following docs/03-report-pages.md:

  • Page 1 — Executive Summary (KPI cards, maturity by entity, type × entity, raised vs closed, attention list).
  • Page 2 — Findings by Type (type cards, type × severity matrix, ageing bar, detail table).
  • Page 3 — Ownership (scorecard, top overdue owners, escalation table with line manager).
  • Page 4 — Risk Heat Map and Risk Candidates (heat map or theme score table, candidate table, findings-by-theme bar, governance note).
  • Hidden page — Finding Detail, with drill-through on Finding_ID (plus Control, Entity, Theme if you want).
  • Sync the global slicers (Entity, Year, Type, Severity, Theme) across pages 1–4.
  • Apply RAG conditional formatting from docs/05-theme-and-style.md. Lock NC / OFI / Gap / OBS colours so they do not shuffle.
  • Add the “As at” label and a “Reset slicers” bookmark if you have more than two slicers.
  • Turn off visual headers (filter / focus icons) on the executive page if you will present it full-screen.

docs.title: G. Quality pass
docs.text:
• Refresh from the sample file and from a copy of your live file (data removed or anonymised if needed) and compare counts to Excel (COUNTA / COUNTIFS on open, overdue, closed).
  • Test a year slicer and a month on the raised-versus-closed visual: closed counts must use the inactive Closed Date relationship, not Raised Date.
  • Test drill-through from a bar, a matrix cell and a table row.
  • Publish a test to a non-production workspace and open the report in the service: confirm the theme, the date table and the slicer sync survived publish.
  • If the source is on SharePoint, configure a scheduled refresh and confirm the gateway or cloud connection succeeds.
  • Remove any remaining sample-only columns (Data_Flag) from visuals. Keep them in the model only if you need to stop sample and live rows being mixed.

docs.title: H. Publish
docs.text:
• Agree the workspace, audience and whether the report is a workspace app or a shared report.
  • Sensitivity label and endorsement (if your tenant uses them): this is typically internal management information, not public.
  • Set refresh (daily is usually enough for an audit tracker; do not promise real-time).
  • Share with view access first. Keep build permission to the people who own the ISMS reporting.
  • Add a short “how to read this” note on page 1 or in the workspace description, including the point that risk candidates are not automatically raised on the register.

docs.title: Reuse and customisation
docs.text:
To reuse this as a template for another programme or another entity set:

  1. Copy the .pbix (once you have one) or start from this repository again.
  2. Change pWorkbookPath and, if needed, the four sheet-name parameters.
  3. Update the column map and the rename steps in Power Query. Do not rename measures to match an idiosyncratic source heading.
  4. Update the entity prefix list in the maturity unpivot. Add or remove entities in Dim Entity, including a Group row if you have central owners.
  5. Retune _Param * measures if the other programme uses a different maturity scale, SLA or clustering rule. Record the values you chose in the management-review pack.
  6. Replace the theme only if the other programme already has a mandated palette; otherwise keep this one so RAG language stays consistent.
  7. Do not paste live data into the sample workbook. Keep sample-data/ fictional so it remains a safe demo.
  8. If you need a fifth page (for example incidents or supplier findings), add a new fact on the same dimensions. Do not merge those rows into Fact Findings unless they truly share the same grain and type list.

docs.title: Regenerating the sample data
docs.text:
From the repository root, with Python 3 and openpyxl installed:

python3 scripts/generate_sample_data.py

This overwrites sample-data/Continual_Improvement_Plan_SAMPLE.xlsx and the CSV copies. All generated rows are flagged Fictional sample.

docs.title: Common problems
docs.text: Symptom Likely cause What to do Closed-in-month is always blank or equals raised-in-month Closed Date relationship is missing or still inactive in the measure Use USERELATIONSHIP as in Closed Findings In Period Maturity does not filter by theme Dim Risk Theme is not related via Dim Control Add the theme-to-control relationship Unpivot exploded into unreadable columns Unexpected prefix or a comment column in the block Restrict the unpivot to known prefixes; park odd columns in a leftovers query % Closed On Time is blank No closed rows, or Closed_Date stored as text Set the type to Date; check Status mapping Repeat-NC flag never fires Entity names differ between Findings and Maturity (UK vs United Kingdom) Harmonise in Power Query using Dim Entity Refresh fails for colleagues Path is a local C:\Users\... file Move the workbook to SharePoint and change the parameter Theme import rejected Invalid JSON Re-validate theme/powerbi-theme.json (no comments, no trailing commas)

docs.title: Downloads
docs.text: All of the build artefacts can be downloaded from this page, or browsed in the repository. The sample workbook and CSVs are fictional and must not be used as live evidence.

docs.title: Sample data
docs.text:
File Description Continual_Improvement_Plan_SAMPLE.xlsx Four-tab sample workbook: Internal Audit Findings (~60 fictional findings), Control Maturity (ISO 27001:2022 Annex A, 93 controls × four example countries), Risk Theme Mapping, and Owners findings.csv CSV copy of Internal Audit Findings control_maturity.csv CSV copy of Control Maturity (wide layout, before the Power Query unpivot) risk_theme_mapping.csv CSV copy of Risk Theme Mapping owners.csv CSV copy of Owners generate_sample_data.py Script that regenerates the workbook and CSVs

To regenerate the sample files from the repository root (Python 3 with openpyxl):

pip install -r scripts/requirements.txt
python3 scripts/generate_sample_data.py

The four example entities in the sample are United Kingdom, Spain, France and Germany. Treat them as placeholders for any <Entity> grain you report on.

docs.text: File Description powerbi-theme.json Importable Power BI theme (View → Browse for themes). Palette and RAG rules are described in Theme and style.

docs.title: DAX measures
docs.text: File Description measures.dax Full measure set (open, overdue, on-time closure, ageing, type counts, maturity, ownership, risk-candidate flags and heat-map scores), with comments. Paste into a measures table in Power BI Desktop.

docs.title: Power Query (M) scripts
docs.text:
Copy these into blank queries in Power BI Desktop after creating the parameters. Details are in the data model and the build checklist.

File Query name 01-parameters.m Parameters and a source-workbook staging note 02-findings.m Fact Findings 03-control-maturity.m Fact Control Maturity (unpivots entity blocks) 04-date-table.m Dim Date 05-controls.m Dim Control 06-entities.m Dim Entity 07-owners.m Dim Owner 08-risk-themes.m Dim Risk Theme

The same files live in powerquery/ in the repository.
